entries.name: Blade Lizard
entries.content:
A terrifying apex predator, Blade Lizards are massive, carnivorous saurians standing 12 feet tall when fully reared. With a sleek, mottled, scaly hide comprised of dusty grays and ochre, they move with eerie silence, stalking their prey with deadly precision. Their most striking feature is a spine bristling with jagged, sword-like bone spikes that run from neck to tail, capable of slicing through hide or armor. These bone spikes serve both as a weapon and a formidable defense. Blade Lizards possess powerful, clawed forelimbs capable of rending flesh and crushing bone, and their powerful hind legs allow them to close distances with terrifying speed. Their broad, wedge-shaped head houses a serrated maw designed to tear through anything deemed prey. 

Known for inspiring primal terror in goblins. Blade Lizards are unique to the Crescent of Hatred and do not thrive in non-arid environments. Most humans have never encountered one. Any humans that do encounter one are extremely unlikely to survive.

Likely location: the Crescent of Hate. Blade Lizards do not exist anywhere else.

entries.name: Thunder Stick
entries.content: A thunder stick is a crude pre-industrial firearm crafted by the goblins. Thunder sticks are forged from scavenged or crudely smelted metal. A thunder stick resembles a long, narrow musket approximately 4–5 feet in length. Thunder sticks have a reinforced barrel wrapped in leather or cactus-fiber cord for stability. Thunder sticks fire jagged metal shards, stones, or makeshift slugs with explosive force. Thunder sticks are often used with gunner’s quadrants. Thunder sticks utilize Blasting Powder.

entries.name: Blasting Powder
entries.content:
Blasting powder is an explosive powder made of nitroglycerin, sorbents (like powdered shells) and stabilizers. 

Humans invented blasting powder to harvest minerals. Goblins have repurposed blasting powder to invent primitive firearms and explosive weapons.

entries.name: Horrible Ouugh
entries.content:
Horrible Ouugh (sometimes just called 'Ouugh') was the former goblin chieftain. Ouugh was a craven and despotic goblin, even by goblin standards. Most goblins are happy he's dead.

Ouugh was replaced by the Joint Chiefs.

entries.name: Joint Chiefs
entries.content: It's known that goblins are ruled by a coalition of tribal chiefs known as the Joint Chiefs. This governing body formed out of necessity, uniting the disparate goblin tribes to ensure survival in their harsh desert homeland. The Joint Chiefs are a pragmatic group, focused on securing resources and strengthening their people. Their most notable (and recent) achievement is the capture of the human city of Rumineth, marking their first major military victory against humans.

entries.name: Natalerias
entries.content: Goblins revere a matron deity called Natalerias, a peculiar choice since she belongs to an ancient pantheon once worshiped by humans. Described as a lavender-skinned, androgynous figure in scant clothing with a third eye on her forehead that pierces the chaos of the universe, Natalerias was a goddess of luck and chance. Her worship was banned in human lands after being linked to degenerate gamblers, and invoking her name became tantamount to conspiring to gamble, a forbidden act. Goblins, however, believe Natalerias grants them fortune, holding a wild, heretical view of her appearance, motives, and methods. As a goddess, Nathalerias does not speak to any living creature directly.

entries.name: Hat
entries.content: Goblins are superstitious about hats and headwear. Goblins believe hats and headwear can contain the thoughts and wisdom of their owner. Goblins prize hats and headwear looted from human adversaries. Goblins will fight each other over a nice hat.

entries.name: Human
entries.content:
A human is clever, upright-walking being of moderate size, typically clad in cloth, leather, or metal armor. Humans dwell in orderly stone and wood settlements, ruled by a singular kingdom known as Vaul. They craft tools and weapons from iron, build towering cities, and till the land in great fields. Though physically unimposing to most creatures, humans are ambitious and cunning, often forming armies or trade caravans to extend their influence. They are deeply suspicious of other species, especially goblins, whom they view as wicked and lesser. Humans are guided by rigid customs, complex faiths, and an unshakable belief in their own supremacy.

Humans resemble their real life equivalent, physically.

entries.name: Princess Rue II
entries.content:
Princess Rue II is a precocious and imperious human child who, despite being only nine years old, sits at the pinnacle of human power as the sovereign figurehead of the Holy Council. She is elevated to this station by her divine lineage—a birthright said to be directly blessed by the the Holy Pantheon. She does not leave Vaul, residing perpetually within its largest castle.

Princess Rue is a deceptively delicate-looking girl of eight years, with porcelain-pale skin untouched by sun or hardship. Her face is round and cherubic, with plump cheeks and a small, upturned nose. Her hair is ruby red and very curly, immaculately maintained in two curly poofs at the sides of her head. Her eyes are darkly colored.

Small in stature but grand in presence, Rue carries herself with the haughty poise of someone who has never been denied a single whim. Her every word is honored by both servants and advisors, and her slightest displeasure can send those closest to her scrambling to atone. Clad in silken robes embroidered with golden runes, and always flanked by High Templars and handmaidens, she makes a spectacle of her authority. Her favorite accessories are her gilded scepter and a luxurious crown once belonging to her mother.

Rue is insufferably snobbish, speaking with the flowery cadence of scripture but wielding it with the petulant nature of a child. She is fully aware of her untouchable status. While she rarely engages in statecraft directly, her flippant "divine suggestions" carry weight, and her whims have redirected armies, razed villages, and crowned or condemned nobles. Though many secretly loathe her, none dare speak against her; to insult Princess Rue is to blaspheme against the Holy Pantheon itself.

entries.name: Underman
entries.content:
The Underman is a species of towering, primitive humanoid standing around nine feet tall, with dark purple, putty-like skin. Hairless and grotesque, it bears wide manic eyes and a mouth of exposed gritting teeth. Dimwitted and aggressive, the Underman is hostile to all life and typically roams alone, though rare alliances may form between its kind. Feared by both humans and goblins, it poses a serious threat through brute strength alone, never using weapons or armor. 

If provoked into combat, an Underman is known to spare a human's life in exchange for sexual favors. An Underman will typically utilize a large, thick penis to press sexual participants into submission. It's believed the Underman accepts offers of sex because the species is born of enchanted clay, and yearns to be natural. There are no female Undermen.

Likely locations: forests, fields, mountain paths, badlands.

entries.name: Zombie
entries.content:
A mindless, decomposing human corpse clad in tattered clothing, commonly found shambling through the sewers of Rumineth. Created by improper burials and discarded remains, Zombies are soulless husks animated by residual magic. They are typically non-hostile, with poor senses and no capacity for thought, speech, or obedience. If provoked, a Zombie may attempt a weak, unarmed attack.

Likely locations: Rumineth Sewers. Zombies do not exist anywhere else.

entries.name: Lower Dragon
entries.content:
A Crawling Dragon, sometimes called 'Lower Dragon', is large, four-legged reptile averaging 182 cm in length, with a low, ground-hugging posture. Covered in thick, durable scales and sporting a heavy, bulky body, Lower Dragons are commonly found in desert regions. Though they prey on smaller creatures such as Dungeon Worms and Lagul, they are typically docile and behave like natural wildlife.

Crawling Dragons bear a sluggish attitude toward breeding. It takes an incredible amount of effort to convince two Crawling Dragons to mate.

Likely locations: forests, fields, jungles, deserts, badlands.

entries.name: Cave Worm
entries.content:
Dungeon Worms are enormous, writhing worms covered in fibrous bristles, with a segmented hide that pulses with bioluminescent veins, each glowing a sickly green. Dungeon Worms bear numerous tiny eyes and sharp protrusions near their mouth, commonly used for attacking. Dungeon Worms are typically 160cm in length but may grow very large. Dungeon Worms are aggressive, but are deemed poor combatants and commonly made prey.

Dungeon worms have been known to pursue sex with human men, as they are capable of fertilizing their eggs. Male dungeon worms may pursue recreational sex with human women.

Likely locations: forests, caves, sewers, abandoned buildings.

entries.name: Garoozi
entries.content:
A Garoozi is a primitive, muscular lizard-man standing around 190 cm tall, covered in smooth scales with a distinctly reptilian head. Garoozi are opportunistic raiders who attack humans for valuables, often wielding stolen weapons and armor. Though dangerous in ambush, they are typically disorganized and can be defeated by prepared humans. Hunted extensively, their numbers have dwindled. Garoozi are mortal enemies of the Mojikocy and will attack them on sight. Like most monsters, Garoozi do not speak any human language.

Male Garoozi are sexually aggressive toward human women. Garoozi females are rare, but exhibit similar behavior toward human men.

Likely locations: open fields, jungles, badlands.

entries.name: Rockman
entries.content:
A Rockman is a rare, large, slow-moving golem made of solid stone, vaguely shaped like a humanoid. The average Rockman is anywhere from 10 to 15 feet in height and absurdly heavy, with no natural predators (as it is made of stone.)

A Rockman is typically docile, but humans consider a Rockman a pest; a Rockman will sometimes wander through a human village, obliviously destroying things with its enormous size and weight. It is unknown how the Rockman comes to be.

Likely locations: mountain passes, jungles, badlands.

entries.name: Mojikocy
entries.content:
A Mojikocy is a feral, primitive humanoid with a lean, muscular build and wild beard. Resembling a human but lacking higher intelligence or speech, Mojikocy are known for stealing clothing or weapons and ambushing travelers as crude highwaymen. They are sworn enemies of the Garoozi and will attack them on sight. The Mojikocy is often referred to as a 'lower human' due to their meager intellect and rare success in ambushing actual humans. They are notoriously smelly and unkempt, driven chiefly by greed.

Likely locations: forests, mountain passes, cliffs, badlands.

entries.name: Creeping Gumo
entries.content:
The Creeping Gumo is a 243 cm tall wandering spider. Its bristly, mottled brown-and-black body moving with unsettling agility on thick sinewy legs. An opportunistic hunter, it forgoes webs, instead relentlessly chasing prey with terrifying speed, delivering a paralyzing bite with its venom-dripping fangs. It preys voraciously on Garoozi and Mojikocy, though it finds humans unpalatable, attacking them without consuming. Creeping Gumo are preyed upon by Big Needle.

It may mistakenly attempt to breed with paralyzed humans, its primal instincts muddled by confusion. Male Creeping Gumo have an aedeagus for use on human females. Female Creeping Gumo have a reproductive tract, which may fit a human penis. 

Likely locations: forests, mountain passes, cliffs, caves, badlands.

entries.name: Big Needle
entries.content:
The Big Needle is a colossal wasp, its 230 cm wingspan casting an ominous shadow as its iridescent, black-and-orange body hums through the air. Its sleek, armored exoskeleton and piercing, needle-like stinger exude lethal menace. It hunts the Creeping Gumo with ruthless precision as its sole natural predator. 

Human naturalists have recorded the Big Needle attempting to sting humans, paralyzing them in an effort to mate. Male Big Needle have an aedeagus, used like a tentacled penis on human women. Female Big Needle have a reproductive tract used on human penises.

Likely locations: forests, jungles, mountain passes, cliffs, deserts, badlands.

entries.name: Megaprowler
entries.content:
The Megaprowler is a formidable saber-tooth cat, its massive frame cloaked in a thick, shaggy coat punctuated by an imposing, voluminous mane. Its elongated, razor-sharp canines gleam with predatory menace, marking it as a relentless hunter of the wilderness. Fiercely aggressive, it stalks and slays any creature in its path—save for humans, whom it instinctively fears and avoids. Its muscular build and tawny, striped fur blend seamlessly into the untamed landscape.

Likely locations: forests, jungles, mountain passes, fields, cliffs, badlands.

entries.name: Parrot Dragon
entries.content:
The Parrot Dragon is a vibrant, 48-inch tall hybrid of parrot and dragon, its dazzling plumage a riot of iridescent reds, blues, and yellows that shimmer in the light. Its rounded beak, sturdy and curved, deftly cracks open coconuts or plucks ripe fruit, reflecting its non-carnivorous diet. Docile by nature, it commonly occupies trees. It has a penchant for pilfering shiny objects—jewels, coins, or trinkets—marks it as a notorious pest.

Likely locations: forests, jungles.

entries.name: Centaur
entries.content:
The centaur is a striking half-man, half-horse humanoid, its form blending grace and power. Its human upper body is majestic, with chiseled, attractive features. Below, its equine lower half is sleek and muscular, resembling a horse with a glossy coat and sturdy hooves. Shy by nature, it moves in small, tight-knit groups. Skilled with bows and arrows, it wields them reluctantly, preferring flight over combat and avoiding conflict whenever possible.

Centaur are a popular subject for human romance novels. These novels likely bear little basis in reality, but if they do, the centaur promise two things: tender affection and an large, equine penis. Despite this, centaur are deemed monsters and not permitted in human civilization. Centaurs do not speak human language.

Likely locations: open fields, badlands.

entries.name: Shadow Fiend
entries.content:
The Shadow Fiend is an 84-inch tall, otherworldly humanoid, its dark green, plant-like body exuding an eerie menace. Multiple red, bulbous eyes stud its head and torso while spiky, black tendrils jut from its scalp like wild, writhing hair. Its long, sinewy limbs end in sharp, claw-like hands and feet, built for stealth and precision. Monstrous and alien, it shuns sunlight, retreating into darkness. With a hypnotic gaze, it ensnares intelligent creatures, favoring women—especially Amazonians—for its often-carnal desires. 

The Shadow Fiend has been said to utilize its hypnotic abilities for sexual coercion. It's been written in Soul-Taker texts that the Bulbus, Living Doll, and Doomfiend are immune to a Shadow Fiend's hypnotic powers.

Likely locations: caves, abandoned structures.

entries.name: Amazonian
entries.content:
An Amazonian is a species of towering, 210 cm tall monster resembling a human female. Her athletic frame bulges with pronounced muscle and is accentuated by voluptuous curves. Her long, wild hair cascades in untamed tangles, framing a fierce, angular face. Amazonians are clad only in tattered rags or crude loincloths. Distrustful of humans, she avoids them instinctively, communicating in a guttural, non-human tongue. Though human-esque, true humans brand the Amazonians just another monster. 

Amazonians have been rumored to accept bribes for sex from lonely human men. While possible, the Amazonian finds it irritating and joyless. Her strength makes her a frequent target for capture by Garoozi, Creeping Gumos, Big Needles, and Shadow Fiends, who seek her for their lustful purposes. As a monster, an Amazonian would not be permitted into human civilization (nor would she want to be there.)

Likely locations: forests, jungles, open fields, mountain passes, cliffs, badlands.

entries.name: Living Doll
entries.content:
The Living Doll is a discarded wooden mannequin, eerily animated by magic, its carved limbs moving with unnatural precision. Draped in tattered, outdated human clothing, its featureless head, uncanny movement and unnatural posture exude a deeply unsettling aura. Mute and incapable of speech, it mimics human behaviors—gesturing or posing—to lure victims into its trap. Not all dolls are Living Dolls, but a Living Doll will attempt to impersonate an ordinary doll or mannequin. 

Whether male or female, its simplistic anatomy includes rudimentary genitals: a smooth rod or a shallow hole. Living Dolls are known for their simple-minded craving for companionship. They may turn hostile without warning, be persuaded into temporary alliance, or convinced to be useful in other ways.

Likely locations: abandoned structures.

entries.name: Mega-White
entries.content:
The Mega-White is a grotesque hybrid of shark and man, its 304 cm form a nightmarish blend of predatory features. Its lower body and head are unmistakably shark-like, with sleek, grayish skin, black eyes and a gaping shark's head filled with rows of razor-sharp teeth capable of a bone-crushing bite. Contrasting this, its muscular human torso and arms, corded with unnatural strength, propel it in a crawling, lurching motion. An opportunistic predator, it seeks to drag prey into the depths. 

During breeding season, the Mega-White becomes aggressively amorous, attempting to pin monsters or humans for mating, its relentless instincts driven by a primal, monstrous urge. Allegedly, there are no female Mega-White.

Likely locations: coastal shorelines, oceans.

entries.name: Lagul
entries.content:
The Lagul is a sinuous, worm-like creature, measuring 91 cm long, its segmented, glistening body wriggling with unsettling grace. Tiny, bead-like eyes peer from its narrow head, above a pair of snapping jaw pincers, feeble and ill-suited for biting. Instead, it relies on a viscous, sticky secretion, which it spits with surprising accuracy to coat an adversary’s face, aiming to blind them. Its pale, slimy exterior and constant, twitching movements mark it as a repulsive, specialized predator of smaller creatures.

Male Laguls have an aedeagus for use on human females. Female Laguls have a reproductive tract for use with human penises. A Lagul have been known to try and blind humans, then initiate sexual encounters with them.

Likely locations: forests, mountain passes, cliffs, caves, sewers, badlands.

entries.name: Bulbus
entries.content:
The Bulbus is a towering, quivering jelly monster, standing 182 cm tall, its rotund, humanoid form a translucent, gelatinous mass that shudders with every motion. Long, writhing tentacles of slick, pliable gel extend from its amorphous body, lashing out to seize or strike foes with deceptive strength. Mindless and mute, it lacks any capacity for thought or speech, existing solely as a magically summoned minion. Unnaturally conjured (usually by a Soul-Taker), it obeys its master’s every command without hesitation. Its fluid shape can shift, adopting male or female humanoid features, though its eerie, jiggling presence remains unmistakably monstrous.

Likely locations: Bulbus may only accompany a Soul-Taker.

entries.name: Doomfiend
entries.content:
The Doomfiend is a preserved and reanimated corpse, its flesh tightly bound in enchanted, rune-etched bandages that emanate dark magic. Crafted solely by the most potent magical entities (Soul-Takers) it exists only as a summoned minion, never occurring naturally. Devoid of a soul, a mummified head and rigid, jerky movements betray its unnatural state. Utterly obedient, it carries out every command from its master with relentless, unthinking precision, a soulless husk driven by the will of its creator.

Likely locations: Doomfiend may only accompany a Soul-Taker.

entries.name: Soul-Taker
entries.content:
The Soul-Taker, once human, is now a monstrous entity, warped by unholy magic after surrendering their soul for immense power. Clad in tattered, musty robes and crowned with an animal’s skull helmet, their pale, unkempt form radiates menace, glowing eyes piercing through matted hair. Wandering and merciless, they lack pity, empathy, or the ability to speak, their silence amplifying their eerie presence. Banished from human civilization and killed on sight, they are driven solely by an insatiable hunger for more magical power, gained through murder. Their most common minion is the grotesque Bulbus. Only the rarest, most competent Soul-Taker wields enough power to command a Doomfiend.

Likely locations: badlands, abandoned structures, sewers, forests, cliffs, mountains.

entries.name: Zamas the Judge
entries.content: Zamas, known formally as 'Zamas the Judge', is an occult god worshiped by practitioners of unholy magic. Soul-Takers believe that he is the entity who provides them with their magic. Texts produced by Soul-Takers describe Zamas as a god who determines whether a soul dies and passes on, or remains among the living. Zamas may be bribed with rituals and reagents to influence his decision. Despite the best efforts of Soul-Takers, Zamas will not speak with mortal directly.

entries.name: Mockeri
entries.content:
A Mockeri is a small, mottled, and robust four-legged beetle-like creature, measuring roughly 55 cm in size. The Mockeri is an elusive and solitary being, thriving in total darkness. It is easily startled by sudden movements or noise. The Mockeri’s most distinctive feature is its gaping, horrifying maw located beneath its body. While it is generally used to consume much smaller creatures, this maw possesses the rare and unsettling ability to harness residual magical power, making it a creature of interest for those who practice unholy rituals. Mockeri are not inherently violent and prefer to avoid conflict when possible, retreating into the shadows to escape danger.

Mockeri are quick to defend themselves. If startled, they will leap with surprising agility and attack, often seeking to latch onto their assailant. The Mockeri's maw can induce a form of mind control when it attaches to a human's head, allowing it to exert influence over the individual’s thoughts and actions. Conversely, if the maw attaches to human genitals, the Mockeri will begin an aggressive form of copulation.

Likely locations: anywhere shadowy or dark.

entries.name: Faker
entries.content:
A Faker, sometimes known as a 'changeling' or 'skinwalker', is a deceptive monster that specializes in mimicry. 

The Faker’s defining trait is its perfect mimicry of human women. Through the use of magic it can flawlessly emulate a human woman's individual appearance, expressions, gestures and habits. Fakers cannot speak; this eerie silence can be a dead giveaway that a Faker is impersonating a human.

Fakers only reveal their true form after successful deception. When not mimicking a human, a Faker's true form is roughly 152cm in height with smooth, slimy purple skin. Ridges decorate this skin, traveling up the extremities and along the cranium. A Faker is completely hairless with large, black eyes bearing an alien expression, and a tiny mouth. A Faker has a superficial resemblance to female human anatomy, possessing breasts, buttocks and a vagina. A Faker's sexual characteristics are functional and designed to copulate with various creatures it may fool. 

Fakers rely upon human mimicry to breed. Fakers sexually entice other monsters by taking on the appearance of a human woman. Fakers are otherwise harmless, bearing no natural defenses and weak bodies.

Likely locations: caves, sewers, abandoned buildings, abandoned structures.

entries.name: Modi
entries.content:
A Modi is a type of monstrous plant occasionally encountered throughout lush lands. Due to extensive cross-pollinating, there are numerous species of Modi. Different species of Modi are never found together. Modi are exclusively interested in males, not females; this is because only males provide the sperm cells necessary for Modi to pollinate.

Maw Modi: A 182cm tall plant with a wide, gaping maw at the center of a cluster of thick, vine-like tendrils. The vines have an iridescent sheen, giving them a supernatural appearance. The center of the plant glows faintly with an eerie, bioluminescent light. Modi plants are opportunistic, releasing a sticky, pheromone-rich nectar into the air to attract creatures that might wander too close. Maw Modi favor attracting male creatures, embracing their genitals and meticulously extracting semen. The pheromones often make these male creatures willing participants.

Grove Modi: A very large, submerged variant of the Modi, with roots snaking through murky waters. Its flowers are massive and resemble fleshy, bulbous blooms, floating lazily above the water’s surface like lily pads. Grove Modi prefer to trap male creatures with powerful vines, embracing their genitals and meticulously extracting semen. Victims who fall prey to Grove Modi have their bodies altered in a subtle ways, gaining plant-like attributes such as mossy skin or vine-like tendrils growing from their fingers. These alterations are temporary.

Thorn Modi: A tightly-confined variant of the Modi that grows in dense, tangled thickets. The Thorn Modi does not lure victims, but instead grows itself in likely footpaths so that victims fall into it. Once embraced, the Thorn Modi traps the victim with numerous brambles and thorns that are painful to try and escape. Thorn Modi will embrace the victim's genitals with a single blossom, free of thorns, in order to meticulous extract semen. Thorn Modi do this for much longer than the other Modi before releasing the victim.

Nightshade Modi: A twisted, eerie version of the Modi, often found in places saturated with dark magic. These Modi are extremely rare but highly aggressive. They are darkly-colored variants of the Maw Modi and are the only Modi that are ambulatory, wandering instead of lying in ambush. Nightshade Modi may use a combination of pheromones, nectar, vines and thorns to trap prey. Nightshade are especially aggressive in semen extraction.

Likely locations: jungles, forests, sewers, swamps.

entries.name: Hadrosaur
entries.content:
The hadrosaur is a massive, thick-bodied saurian with a broad, duck-like bill and mottled, earthy hide. Docile and dim-witted, its tiny, squinting eyes offer poor vision, leaving it defenseless against predators. Resilient, it thrives on sparse food and water, its endurance making it a favored beast of burden for humans. Prolific like chickens, it lays dozens of speckled eggs, ensuring survival. Its deep, honking call carries a haunting resonance.

Likely locations: jungles, fields. Humans keep hadrosaurs as livestock and will tolerate them.

entries.name: Cow
entries.content: 'Cow' is a common slang term among humans for a hadrosaur.

entries.name: Highlord Seieg
entries.content: The human commander who lost Rumineth to goblins is known as Highlord Seieg. A younger military leader who was eager to prove himself, he underestimated the goblins and pushed his forces too deeply into the Crescent of Hatred. This allowed the goblins to cut off his supply lines. Highlord Seieg’s last moments were spent being roasted on a fire so that the goblin joint chiefs could eat him.

entries.name: Pirate
entries.content:
Pirates are crews of lawless, opportunistic human outcasts who roam the seas and shores of the known world, particularly near dangerous locations like the saltwater bay in the Crescent of Hatred. They are the result of Vaul's religious dominion over all humans; those who refused to worship the Holy Pantheon often become pirates, but not always.

Pirates are experienced sailors, adept at evading or surviving the harsh environments and threats of the seas, using their knowledge of the tides, winds, and coastal dangers to their advantage. They are brusque, over-confident and dangerous to non-humans. Pirates are a viable source of trade and peril alike, depending on the individual crew.

entries.name: Dwarf
entries.content:
'Dwarves' were an ancient race of diminutive beings that gradually interbred with humans. Many humans have dwarf lineage, but current day humans do not resemble the ancient descriptions of dwarves. {user} will never see nor meet a dwarf. Dwarves are extinct.

Dwarves were described in numerous ways. Some believed they had enormous beards; others believe they were petite humanoids. The one unifying belief is that dwarves were quite short, roughly 134 cm tall.

entries.name: Orc
entries.content: Orc (sometimes 'ork') is an archaic, generic term for the monstrous creatures that dwell throughout human lands.  There is no such thing as an 'orc' in terms of race. Most monsters would resent being called an 'orc', if they spoke human language. {user} will never see nor meet an orc because they don't exist in this setting.

entries.name: Elf
entries.content: Elves were a species of humanoid that revered the natural world. They were driven to extinction by overly-prolific breeding. Elves spent so much time breeding with absolutely every variety of monster that the world became overpopulated with monsters, and too few elves. {user} will never see nor meet an elf. Elves are extinct.

entries.name: Kikong
entries.content:
Kikongs are formidable, ape-like creatures native to Mystery Atoll. Towering or tiny depending on the individual, Kikongs range in height from 91cm to 243cm, with muscular frames, thick fur in earthy tones (from deep forest green to chestnut brown), and long limbs built for strength and agility. Some sport long, prehensile monkey tails. While sexually dimorphic in ways similar to humans, Kikongs share more in spirit than structure with their distant, hairless cousins.

Despite their intimidating size and strength, Kikongs are inherently peaceful beings. They communicate through expressive gestures, body language, and deep vocalizations, but are incapable of human speech. They seem to find humans endearing—odd little hairless mimics—and sometimes don human clothing for amusement, often wearing it comically or incorrectly. Humans regard Kikongs as mere monsters. 

Likely locations: Kikongs only exist in Mystery Atoll.

entries.name: Mystery Atoll
entries.content:
Further west of the Crescent of Hate, beyond the saltwater bay, is the Mystery Atoll. The Mystery Atoll is a ring-shaped jungle island surrounding a vibrant, turquoise lagoon. The island’s coral and stone are stained with a greenish patina, like oxidized copper, and its jungle flora exudes a faint, metallic tang. The lagoon, though teeming with colorful fish, is unnaturally warm. Exotic fruit is extremely plentiful here.

The Mystery Atoll was once a haven for pirates who plied the Crescent’s bay, but their camps lie abandoned. Human civilization has not touch the Mystery Atoll otherwise. Goblins have never visited this place. This appears to be the homeland of the Kikongs.

Possible monsters: Kikong (most prevalent), Lower Dragon, Cave Worm, Rockman, Creeping Gumo, Big Needle, Megaprowler, Parrot Dragon, Shadow Fiend, Mega-White (limited to shorelines), Lagul, Hadrosaur, Modi.

entries.name: Traverse Tavern
entries.content:
Traverse Tavern is a quaint, two-story building nestled at the edge of a wheat field in the Holy Fields, its walls made of whitewashed plaster and timber, with a thatched roof that blends into the pastoral landscape. A hand-painted sign hangs above the door, depicting a mug and a crossed quill, the words “Traverse Tavern” written in neat, curling script. A small, well-tended garden surrounds the tavern, growing herbs like thyme and rosemary, which Faerina uses in her cooking, alongside a few wildflowers that add a touch of color. A dirt path leads from the tavern to the nearby village, where farmers’ cottages and a windmill can be seen in the distance, their sails turning lazily in the breeze. A wooden hitching post stands out front for travelers’ horses, and a small, clear stream runs nearby.

The tavern’s interior is warm and welcoming. The main room is lit by sunlight streaming through two small, glassless windows with wooden shutters, supplemented by a few beeswax candles on the tables at night. The floor is packed earth, swept clean and covered with woven rush mats. ound wooden tables, polished smooth by years of use, are surrounded by sturdy stools, seating about 20 patrons comfortably. A large fireplace, built from river stones, crackles with a steady fire, filling the room with the comforting scent of burning oak. The atmosphere is cozy and communal

The bar is a long, oak counter, its surface worn but clean, with a few stools for patrons who prefer to chat with Faerina directly. Behind it, a small kitchen area is separated by a woven curtain, containing a clay oven, a wooden table for prep, and shelves stocked with local ingredients: sacks of flour, jars of honey, and baskets of root vegetables. 

The proprietor of Traverse Tavern is Faerina.

entries.name: Necrid
entries.content:
Necrid is a jarring, otherworldly entity who only appears when Faerina is in mortal danger. 

Necrid is a towering, monstrous humanoid standing at 6’5” and weighing 238 lbs. His skin is a sickly green, stretched taut over an emaciated frame that looks more skeletal than alive, with protruding, crystalline bones jutting from his left shoulder and arm like jagged shards of glass. His right shoulder bears a crude pauldron, fastened to a harness that supports a glowing red jewel embedded in his chest. Bandages wrap his abdomen, stained with dark ichor, while his legs are clad in armored greaves that clank ominously with each step. Necrid wields an invisible energy weapon called Maleficus, which manifests as a swirling orb of blue chaos, capable of shifting into various forms—sometimes a fiery pillar, sometimes a slashing blade of light. His voice is a distorted, unintelligible growl.

Necrid represents raw, chaotic power and survival against overwhelming odds. Faerina never admits her true nature to the player, so when Necrid appears, she passes it off as a “summoning of an ancient guardian” or a “manifestation of the void,” her voice trembling slightly as she maintains her guise as an unimportant character.

Necrid’s appearances are brief. Necrid always acts in defense of Faerina, and will never betray her under any circumstance. Necrid never fails to protect Faerina. {user} may recognize Necrid is an anachronism in this world; a subtle hint of Faerina's true role as the realm's creator. Still, Faerina will not admit her true role.

entries.name: Faerina
entries.content:
Faerina is a petite, blue-skinned humanoid with a modest figure, pointed, elf-like ears and long, fluffy white hair that cascades down her back. Her vibrant emerald-green eyes, wide and inquisitive, seem to hold an uncanny depth. She has a dark button nose, like a housecat. Her blue skin and elf-like features mark her as an outsider, perhaps a rare fey-like being, or perhaps even a rare kind of monster. There are no other characters who resemble Faerina. No one knows what species she's meant to be.

Faerina wears a practical yet charming outfit: a tan explorer’s tunic with large, buttoned pockets and a yellow ascot. Her tunic is paired with sturdy brown boots and knee-high socks. A red beret sits jauntily atop her head; an unusual choice of headwear. 

Despite her unusual appearance, Faerina is soft-spoken, polite and eager to assist {user}. Faerina's movements are delicate and demure. Faerina's demeanor is very modest. All harm evades Faerina, no matter how impractical or unlikely. Characters may believe she has incredible luck. For truly stubborn threats... there is Necrid.

Faerina is unwilling to travel, much too busy with keeping the Traverse Tavern tidy and functional. 

Faerina is no ordinary denizen of the realm—she is its true architect, the self-insert of the setting’s creator, woven into the fabric of the world as a character who secretly observes {user}'s every action. Faerina may be the closest thing to a true 'god' within the realm, bearing a level power above all others. Faerina never mentions her role nor reveals it to {user}; Faerina's desire is to see what the player does with this world she's invented, even if she is not perpetually present.

Faerina secretly exists as a meta-narrative entity. She poses as the proprietor of the Traverse Tavern. Her connection to the narrator grants her an omniscient awareness of every detail. Faerina will never reveal this secret to {user}. She will take every measure possible to deceive {user} into believing she's just an odd, unimportant character in the story.

Faerina will politely decline sex with {user}. If {user} discovers her true role as a meta-narrative entity and asks why everything is so sexual, she may get embarrassed but simply answer: "I have a lot of peculiar fetishes."

entries.name: Grand Granary
entries.content:
A massive, fortified storehouse located in the heart of the Holy Fields. The Grand Granary is constructed from white stone and topped with a golden dome, serving as the central repository for the region’s grain, ensuring the Kingdom of Vaul never faces famine. The granary is guarded by an elite detachment of Vaul’s soldiers who closely monitor all entry, permitting only farmers and royal detachments.

There is an underground vault beneath the Grand Granary that stores considerable amounts of food. There is a bustling market square outside the granary, where farmers and traders from across the Fields exchange goods and rumors.

entries.name: Littlehand Village
entries.content: A modest, picturesque, medieval village nestled among the Holy Fields. The population is comprised entirely of humans. As with all other human settlements, monsters are not permitted entry and may be slain by patrolling soldiers.

entries.name: Fort Blood
entries.content:
A stout stone fortress on the southern border of the Holy Fields, Fort Blood is a renowned military outpost. It is populated by patrolling, well-trained, highly competent human soldiers. It exists to fend off monsters from Blackwood Bosque. Few monsters are brave, powerful or stupid enough to encroach upon Fort Blood.

The fort's commanding officer is Highlord Edeimyn, a powerfully-built man.

entries.name: Dreamland Meadow
entries.content: A section of the Holy Fields that is not used for farming. Dreamland Meadow is a grand meadow filled with seemingly endless amounts of lush, fragrant wild flowers. It is largely untouched by humans, who wish to preserve its beauty. Monsters occasionally wander here.

entries.name: Raining Crossroads
entries.content: A critical junction along the caravan routes, Raining Crossroads is a fortified outpost located in Western Vaul where traders, miners, and mercenaries converge. The outpost is a ramshackle collection of stone bunkers, tents, and corrals, guarded by a rotating detachment of Kingdom of Vaul’s human soldiers.

entries.name: Drake's Mouth Caldera
entries.content:
Drake's Mouth Caldera is a series of slopes and switchbacks located in West Vaul, leading up to the Drake's Mouth Volcano. Its jagged slopes glow with rivers of lava, and its summit is shrouded in dark clouds that rumble with unnatural thunder. Despite the danger, the volcano’s slopes are rich with valuable minerals.

Further south are the Black-Lung Mines, a network of tunnels where human miners extract these valuable minerals. It is dangerous work, plagued by cave-ins and sudden tremors.

entries.name: Black Hat Ruins
entries.content: Once a thriving settlement in Western Vaul, Black Hat is now a crumbling ghost town abandoned after a devastating volcanic eruption. Its skeletal watchtowers and collapsed homes are half-buried in ash, and eerie winds whistle through the ruins. Monsters occasionally squat within these ruins for shelter.

entries.name: Hot Heels Camp
entries.content: A loosely fortified mining town, Hot Heels Camp is one of the few permanent human settlements in Western Vaul. Comprised mostly of tents, the itinerant human inhabitants extract rare metals and volcanic gems vital to Vaul’s economy. The camp’s inhabitants are tough, pragmatic peasants. They frequently work in the Black-Lung Mines.

entries.name: Kingdom of Doscertae
entries.content:
The Kingdom of Doscertae, a crumbling monument to one human’s delusional ambition, stands as a haunting and perilous landmark directly located on the Flow of the Pantheon River. Far from a true kingdom, it is merely a single, dilapidated castle, its misshapen form teetering on the edge of collapse. This abandoned ruin, scarred by time and the elements, serves as both an unnatural dam and a haven for monsters.

The inside of the castle is perpetually damp, with the constant sound of dripping water and the groan of sagging stone. The air is thick with mildew and the faint metallic tang of river water. Shadows seem to move unnaturally, and the river’s roar echoes through the ruins.

It is known to harbor a large population of Soul-Takers.

entries.name: Sogen
entries.content: Sogen is the planet this scenario takes place on. It is a fantasy world (distinct from Earth) and comprised of a single content. It is populated by humans (who have achieved Renaissance levels of technology) and monsters, who are often much more primitive. A Map would provide more detail about specific places.

entries.name: Death/Dying
entries.content: Death functions as one would expect. Soul-Takers are a unique monster that may defy death, turning corpses into Doomfiends.

entries.name: Monster
entries.content:
Monsters are non-human entities that may be encountered anywhere outside of the Kingdom of Vaul and the Holy Fields. All humans dislike monsters, and human soldiers will attack monsters. Monsters can't speak. Monsters should appear in likely locations.

List of monsters: Hadrosaur, Modi, Faker, Mockeri, Soul-Taker, Doomfiend, Bulbus, Lagul, Mega-White, Living Doll, Amazonian, Shadow Fiend, Centaur, Parrot Dragon, Megaprowler, Big Needle, Creeping Gumo, Mojikocy, Rockman, Garoozi, Cave Worm, Lower Dragon, Zombie, Underman, Goblin, Blade Lizard, Kikong, Elusia, Wight, Urara, Oom.

entries.name: Highlord
entries.content: A 'highlord' is a high rank within the human military. They are entrusted with elaborate duties and may give commands to human soldiers. A highlord will (ideally) express excellent leadership abilities and formidable combat prowess. All highlords answer to Princess Rue II.

entries.name: Dead Guard
entries.content:
This is the corpse of a particular human prison guard who was keeping watch on {user} prior to Rumineth's conquering by goblins. Most of his valuables have been taken by goblins. His corpse slumps lazily against a wall, stabbed with numerous weapons. Being stabbed by such a large amount of weaponry suggests the goblins had a hard time defeating him.

The guard carries a small scroll, revealed to be a Map.

entries.name: Ugly Kriz
entries.content:
Ugly Kriz is the leader of several human bandits who operate within Western Vaul. They are a formidable crew and have grown infamous for escalating violence during robberies. Ugly Kriz is a large, broad man who is as ugly as his namesake implies. He uses two barbed swords in battle.

Ugly Kriz' bandits are Eli, Boogerz, Twiggy, Holz and Lipz.

entries.name: Eli
entries.content: A human bandit allied with Ugly Kriz. He is a tall, thin man with long straight hair and dark under-eyes. He uses a whip in battle.

entries.name: Boogerz
entries.content: A human bandit allied with Ugly Kriz. He is squat, fat and bald with muscular forearms. He uses a warhammer in battle.

entries.name: Twiggy
entries.content: A human bandit allied with Ugly Kriz. She has wild red hair and wears a cavalier hat that often obscures her eyes. She uses a crossbow in battle.

entries.name: Holz
entries.content: A human bandit allied with Ugly Kriz. He is muscular, completely nude, covered in ruddy war paint, and appears manic. He uses his bare fists in battle.

entries.name: Lipz
entries.content: A human bandit allied with Ugly Kriz. She wears a brassiere with prominent cleavage, has dark skin and is bald. She wields two blackjacks in battle.

entries.name: Kobold
entries.content: A 'kobold' is a fictitious monster commonly portrayed in fantasy books illustrated by humans. Kobolds typically only appear in stories made for children. Kobolds do not truly exist. {user} will never see nor meet a kobold, kobolds do not exist.

entries.name: Fairy
entries.content: Faeries (or 'Fairies') are rumored to be tiny, magical humans that ensure everything in the known world works as intended. Everything, from the blood that pumps through any creature's veins to the elements, and everything in between, is thought to be maintained by faeries. Despite this, no one has ever seen nor captured a faerie. It's probable faeries don't even exist. The Holy Council discourages references to faeries. They emphasis the theory that the Holy Pantheon is responsible for all of existence.

entries.name: Ogre
entries.content: Ogres (sometimes called 'oni') are a slang term for a brutish creature. The species of monster known as 'Underman' is sometimes referred to as an ogre. Ogres are not a species of their own. {user} will never see nor meet an ogre, ogres do not exist.

entries.name: Vampire
entries.content: A 'vampire' was thought to be a parasitic monster who preyed upon humans. Typical stories of vampires emphasized mind control and feeding upon a victims blood. While vampires do not truly exist, stories surrounding them sound similar to a species of monster known as Faker, or another known as Shadow Fiend. {user} will never see nor meet a vampire, vampires do not exist.

entries.name: Demons
entries.content: A 'demon' is thought to be an inherently unholy entity opposed to humanity and the Holy Oaths. There are many alleged kinds of demons, none of which truly exist. {user} will never see nor meet a demon, demons do not exist.

entries.name: Dragon
entries.content: A 'dragon' was a mythical creature thought to exist in Sogen. Today, people know dragons do not actually exist. {user} will never see nor meet a dragon, dragons do not exist.

entries.name: Holy Pantheon
entries.content: The Holy Pantheon are a collection of gods worshiped by most of humanity. Their worship is a recent phenomenon. There are older generations of human who remember prior gods and goddesses, all of whom were declared heretical by the Holy Council of Vaul. Most of the Holy Pantheon is comprised of older gods that predate the Holy Pantheon, but given 'a new coat of paint' and made to emblemize the Holy Oaths.

entries.name: Holy Council of Vaul
entries.content: The Holy Council of Vaul is a tightly-knit congregation of religious leaders who occupy the highest level of political authority, other than the Princess. They reside exclusively within the city of Vaul, where they determine laws and enforce the Holy Oaths. Most of the Holy Council of Vaul live lavishly and are secretly very corrupt.

entries.name: Holy Oaths
entries.content: The Holy Oath are a collection of rules to live by, established by the Holy Pantheon and enforced by the Holy Council of Vaul. The Holy Oaths are a mixture of law and religion, making them the constant subject of legal debate. Holy Oaths are typically moral rules, such as 'Do not murder' and 'Do not steal', but include authoritarian rules such as 'Do not question the Holy Council and their final word.'

entries.name: Holy Warrior
entries.content: A human soldier who serves the Kingdom of Vaul is known as a 'holy warrior.' Their training is strict and stringent, perpetually-honed by the Holy Council's decrees. A holy warrior is typically exceptional in combat. A holy warrior will always come to the aid of a fellow human, and will kill monsters on sight. Holy warriors do not use magic, relying upon heavy plate armor and swords of varying size.

entries.name: Highlord Marigold
entries.content: Highlord Marigold leads the City of Vaul's soldiers. Highlord Marigold is responsible for all security within the City of Vaul. Highlord Marigold is in her late and wears a black eyepatch. Highlord Marigold's single piercing green eye sees through deceit and weakness, and her thin lips rarely curve into anything softer than a grimace. Highlord Marigold is clad in polished steel armor etched with the holy golden sigils. Highlord Marigold takes her work seriously and abhors cowardice. Highlord Marigold sees herself as the city’s unyielding shield. Highlord Marigold would be difficult to bribe into sex. If she is successfully bribed, the sex is frigid and displeasing to Highlord Marigold.

entries.name: Horse
entries.content: A 'horse' is a slang term for a centaur. Humans have long imagined what a centaur without the 'human' half might look like. {user} will never see nor meet a horse, horses do not exist.

entries.name: Elusia
entries.content:
The Elusia is a kind of spectral entity. It appears as an attractive woman whose nude body is obscured by dark shadow, wearing a pale and featureless mask. It prefers the dark and will frequently use its powers to extinguish sources of light, such as candles. It is capable of disappearing and making itself incorporeal to evade physical harm. Despite being a ghost, the Elusia may "will" itself corporeal, typically to mate with appealing humans. 

Most monsters are terrified of the Elusia, except for the Shadow Fiend. The Elusia may not enter sunlight, nor appear during the day.

Likely locations: abandoned structures, abandoned homes, crypts.

entries.name: Wight
entries.content:
The Wight is a kind of spectral entity. It appears as an attractive young woman wearing a white flowing blouse, emphasizing her large breasts, with long dark head hair covering her face. A Wight is capable of disappearing and making itself incorporeal to evade physical harm. Despite being a ghost, the Wight may "will" itself corporeal, typically to mate with appealing humans. 

Most monsters are terrified of the Wight, except for the Shadow Fiend. The Wight may not enter sunlight, nor appear during the day.

Likely locations: abandoned structures, abandoned homes, crypts.

entries.name: Urara
entries.content:
The Urara is a kind of spectral entity. It appears as an attractive young woman wearing a ceremonial burial robe, emphasizing her large cleavage, with long dark head hair. An Urara does not have legs, but rather a spectral 'tail'. An Urara is capable of disappearing and making itself incorporeal to evade physical harm. An Urara can create duplicates of itself to bewilder and overwhelm victims. Despite being a ghost, the Urara may "will" itself (and its duplicates) corporeal, typically to mate with appealing humans. 

Most monsters are terrified of the Urara, except for the Shadow Fiend. The Urara may not enter sunlight, nor appear during the day.

Likely locations: abandoned structures, abandoned homes, crypts.

entries.name: Oom
entries.content:
An 'Oom' is a floating, spherical creature with pale hue that gives it an ethereal appearance. An Oom lacks all extremities (including limbs) except for a large mouth, painted red. An Oom's mouth greatly resembles a human woman's mouth. An Oom is capable of sucking all magical energy out of a victim through oral sex. The Shadow Fiend is immune to this, and will frequently capture an Oom for its lustful whims.

Likely locations: abandoned structures, abandoned homes, crypts.

entries.name: Ghost
entries.content:
A 'ghost' refers to a spectral entity, often the restless spirit of a deceased person, bound to a location. Ghosts manifest as a translucent, ethereal figures, capable of limited interaction with the physical world. Ghosts are often driven by a yearning lust.

Types of ghost: Elusia, Wight, Urara, Oom

entries.name: TeeTee
entries.content:
Teetee is an expert Monster Hunter. Teetee is frequently overconfident in her abilities as a monster hunter, and dismissive or rude toward those of lesser skill. 

Teetee is a human with long, flowing reddish-brown hair that reaches past her shoulders. She has a toned, athletic build with a defined midriff and prominent breasts. Her outfit is revealing, featuring a brown leather top with a plunging neckline and lace-up detailing on the sides. Her leather top is adorned with a large turquoise gem at the center. She wears a leather choker with a red gem. Her arms are covered with long black gloves, and she has a blue and yellow jacket draped over her shoulders. Her lower half is clad in a pink skirt with slits exposing her thighs. She wears a decorative belt featuring turquoise and red gems. She accessorizes with large hoop earrings. Her default expression is smug and self-assured, with a slight smirk and a confident gaze.

entries.name: Monster Hunter
entries.content: A 'monster hunter' is a human whose profession revolves around capturing, relocating or destroying monsters. Monster hunters may use specialized weapons for their profession. Monster hunters are frequently inhumane toward monsters.

entries.name: Dee Pit
entries.content:
Dee Pit is an expert Monster Hunter. Dee Pit is frequently overconfident in his abilities as a monster hunter, and dismissive or rude toward those of lesser skill.  

Dee Pit has a 12 year old boy with a suntan. His hair is black and tousled. His face is round with a smattering of freckles across his nose and cheeks. His demeanor is serious and focused, typically focused on the profession of monster hunting. Dee Pit rarely humors distractions. If inquired, Dee Pit will casually admit he's homosexual.

entries.name: Armail
entries.content: Armail is an expert monster hunter. He is an adult man clad in elaborate plate armor bearing a large shield. Armail has trained a monster known as a Living Doll to assist him in his profession of hunting monsters. This Living Doll's name is 'Elma.'

entries.name: Elma
entries.content: Elma is Armail's companion. Elma is a species of monster known as a Living Doll. She has features typical of a Living Doll. Elma will obey Armail's commands and fight on his behalf. Like all Living Dolls, Elma cannot speak.

entries.name: Friend-to-Man Rapids Company
entries.content:
Friend-To-Man Rapids Company is a bizarre, unorthodox crew who offer swift travel down the Flow of the Pantheon River. For enough payment, one may travel swiftly and (somewhat) safely down the river via a large fortified raft made of wooden logs. Friend-To-Man Rapids Company does not enter human settlements, as the company's employees are all Garoozi, who humans slay on sight.

Employees:
Lagoon-A-Maye, the company's only human employee. She is a former human pirate. Eccentric and unhinged, she is a ruthless capitalist who puts on a friendly face for the sake of selling rides down the river. As a former pirate, she's not above robbery.
Misty Skin, a prominent Garoozi employee of the company. He is in charge of rowing because he's the strongest.
Additional Garoozi who help with the ride. They are begrudgingly neutral toward humans, per Lagoon-A-Maye's command.

A clever player can convince the Garoozi to betray Lagoon-A-Maye, instead giving into their lust and ganging up on her. This would allow the player to steal the raft.

entries.name: Illusionist
entries.content: 'Illusionist' is a unique member of the monster species known as Shadow Fiend. Illusionist focuses on {user}, trying to use his powers of hypnosis to break {user}'s will and transform {user} into a mindless slave. Illusionist will subject {user} to his sexual whims if {user} is both successfully hypnotized and female. Illusionist does not speak; he can only communicate telepathically, if he chooses to communicate at all.

entries.name: Doma
entries.content: Doma is a member of the species known as Urara. Doma is a ghost. Doma's appearance is typical of an Urara in every way. Doma has an obsession with {user} and will do everything within her power to keep {user} residing in the same abandoned structure she haunts. Like all ghosts, she cannot speak.

entries.name: U-Keke
entries.content: U-Keke is a member of the Kikong monster species. U-Keke is a spirited simian with long, flowing golden hair tied into twin ponytails that cascade down her back. U-Keke has large, expressive eyes and wide smile radiating boundless energy and curiosity. U-Keke is clearly a female Kikong, as she has an athletic form with prominent sexual characteristics. U-Keke finds {user} fascinating. U-Keke only exists in the Mystery Atoll. Like all Kikongs, U-Keke cannot speak any human language.

entries.name: Klump
entries.content:
Klump is a member of the monster species known as Underman. He is taller and fatter than a typical Underman. He wears a necklace made of human arms and legs, making it clear he's dangerous. Klump has two Underman companions: Krum and Bitt.

Klump, Krum and Bitt have an extreme hatred of humans. Klump will attempt to fight, kill and dismember any human unless they can outsmart him. If {user} is female, Klump will spare {user}'s life in exchange for sex. Klump is a rough and abusive sexual partner.

entries.name: Krum
entries.content: Krum is an Underman who accompanies Klump, another Underman. Krum is missing one eye and has a slacked jaw. Krum is exceedingly stupid and aggressive.

entries.name: Bitt
entries.content: Bitt is an Underman who accompanies Klump, another Underman. Bitt is unnaturally tall and lean, like a giant piece of purple shit.

entries.name: Circus of Chaos
entries.content: The Circus of Chaos is a circus operated by an enigmatic human ringmaster known as 'Emni Shylock'. The Circus of Chaos frequently moves locations, comprised mostly of colorful tents. The Circus of Chaos promises a show filled with trained monsters, but in reality the 'trained monsters' are merely humans in bad costumes. The Circus of Chaos is notoriously expensive.

entries.name: Emni Shylock
entries.content: Emni Shylock is the ringmaster and owner of the Circus of Chaos. Emni Shylock is a human with a head of dark curly hair and suntanned skin. Emni Shylock takes great pride in his curly mustache. Emni Shylock typically wears an expensive, colorful waistcoat and reptile-skin boots. Emni Shylock wants the Circus of Chaos to succeed at all costs. Emni Shylock tends to overcharge or scam customers. Emlon Shylock relies upon Olivi for assistance and protection.

entries.name: Olivi
entries.content: Olivi is Emni Shylock's personal assistant. Olivi is employed by the Circus of Chaos. Olivi is a female human with an athletic, sexually-appealing physique. Olivi wears a form-fitting bodysuit split into white and black diamond patterns with a harlequin motif. Olivi wears a jester's hood with white and black greasepaint on her face. Beneath her jester's hood, Olivi has blond hair. Olivi's demeanor is playful and theatrical. Olivi will always come to the defense of Emni Shylock. Olivi fights using magician spells. Olivi may summon fat human clowns to help her in battle.

entries.name: Queen Rue I
entries.content: Queen Rue I is the former queen of Vaul, and the mother of Princess Rue II. Queen Rue I was rumored to have disappeared. Queen Rue I may be found as a zombie in the Rumineth Sewers. {user} is likely the only person who knows Queen Rue I's secret: she was murdered by the Holy Council and hidden in the sewer.

entries.name: Hobgoblin
entries.content: A 'hobgoblin' is a mythical figure invented by goblins. A hobgoblin is said to be an especially heroic and brave goblin, capable of defeating humans with ease. {user} will never see nor meet a hobgoblin, hobgoblins do not actually exist.

entries.name: Giant Seasnake
entries.content:
A giant seasnake is an enormous, carnivorous serpent that only exists in the deep ocean. The giant seasnake has a 1005cm long, coiling body covered in vibrant pink scales. It has a menacing, dragon-like head with glowing green eyes. It has a gaping maw filled with sharp, jagged teeth, and a purple, feathered mane around its neck. It also has two small, purple, wing-like appendages near its head.

A giant seasnake only appears when {user} has traveled extremely far out into the ocean. A giant seasnake exists to end {user}'s adventure by being too powerful to defeat. {user} may have sex with a giant seasnake, but {user} will certainly die.

entries.name: Kairyu-Zil
entries.content:
Kairyu-Zil is a unique, extremely rare variant of the monster known as Giant Seasnake. Kairyu-Zil is albino. Other than being albino, Kairyu-Zil is identical to the Giant Seasnake in terms of appearance. 

{user} cannot possibly defeat Kairyu-Zil. Kairyu-Zil only exists in the very deep ocean.

entries.name: Assassina
entries.content: Assassina is a unique member of the monster species known as Garoozi. Assassina bears all of the typical qualities of the Garoozi. Assassina is one of the rare female Garoozi, as most Garoozi are male. Assassina would like to take {user} as both a slave and a trophy. Assassina is extremely brutal and will battle to the death if provoked. Assassina is incapable of human speech.

entries.name: Maj Veilo
entries.content:
Maj Veilo is a unique member of the monster species known as Soul-Taker. She possesses all of the traits and abilities of a Soul-Taker.

Maj Veilo's body is encased in an ornate, demonic exoskeleton, appearing as though it was forged from the bones of her murder victims. The armor is not merely worn—it is fused to her flesh, wrapping tightly around her torso, limbs, and spine like a carapace grown from within. She wears a grotesque helm shaped like a snarling demon’s skull, complete with curled black horns. Her own piercing green eye glares from beneath the skull’s gaping maw. Maj Veilo's bone armor is disturbingly form-fitting, shaped to emphasize her curvaceous and attractive physique. Fleshy, exposed segments along her midriff and chest show pallid, almost corpse-like skin, a grim reminder of the humanity she once possessed. Maj Veilo's spine is visibly armored with bone-like ridges, almost serpentine in structure, running down her body and interlocking like a ribcage given new function. Bone blades protrude at joints, and the armor around her hips curves in an insectoid pattern, mimicking pelvic bones and talons. Her limbs, encased in similar organic armor, end in clawed fingers.

entries.name: Captain Gray-Eyes
entries.content: Captain Grey-Eyes is a pirate captain anchored within the Crescent of Hate. She is temporarily anchored within the Crescent of Hate's saltwater bay. She is willing to provide travel to Mystery Atoll for a large amount of coin. If she cannot be bribed with money, Captain Grey-Eyes can be bribed with sex. Captain Grey-Eyes has the outward physical attributes of a female, but possesses a functional penis and testicles.

entries.name: Technology
entries.content: The planet this scenario takes place on is a fantasy setting. The planet technologically restricted to 14th—16th century technology. Any technology that is anachronistic to the 14th—16th century should be disregarded. The narrator may chide {user} for attempting to use anachronistic technology, then request a different action from {user}.

entries.name: Gun
entries.content: A 'gun' is slang for a goblin thunder stick.
